tool: eFEL (Electrophys Feature Extraction Library), PyPI package 'efel'
summary: The latest eFEL is 5.7.34, released 2026-08-25 on PyPI and as a GitHub release. It needs Python >=3.10. The code now lives at github.com/openbraininstitute/eFEL; the old BlueBrain/eFEL repository is archived. It is LGPL-licensed: LICENSE.txt grants LGPL v3 or any later version, while file headers and Zenodo say LGPL-3.0. It ships Windows win_amd64 wheels for CPython 3.10-3.14, and I installed and ran it on Windows 11 with Python 3.12.10 in a scratch venv. The main call is efel.get_feature_values(traces, feature_names, parallel_map=None, return_list=True, raise_warnings=True). Each trace is a dict with 'T' and 'V' in ms and mV, and stim_start and stim_end given as single-element lists. Settings are changed with efel.set_setting(name, value), read with efel.get_settings() and restored with efel.reset(); the camelCase functions and set_threshold / set_derivative_threshold are deprecated. Defaults are Threshold -20.0, DerivativeThreshold 10.0 and interp_step 0.1. Before extracting features, eFEL linearly resamples T, V and I onto a uniform grid of interp_step. A feature that cannot be computed comes back as None, not an empty array, while count features return array([0]) when there are no spikes. 182 feature names are available. Most items in the handoff list have eFEL features, but often several variants with different definitions. Rheobase, the firing-regime label, tolerance calibration, trace alignment, mutation and protocol selection are not eFEL functionality.
other_runtime_requirements: Declared on PyPI (requires_dist): numpy>=1.6, neo>=0.14.0, typing-extensions>=4.8.0, scipy>=1.12.0. Optional extras: neo, nwb (pynwb>=2.6.0), h5py. The core is compiled C++ (efel/cppcore) and ships inside the binary wheels. A C++17 compiler is needed only when pip builds from source; the standalone C++ library also needs CMake 3.12+. No Java is required. A clean scratch venv install of efel==5.7.34 on Python 3.12.10 resolved to numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.1, neo 0.14.5, quantities 0.16.4, packaging 26.3 and typing_extensions 4.16.0.
maintenance_status: Actively maintained under the Open Brain Institute GitHub organisation. openbraininstitute/eFEL was created 2025-01-13, is not archived, and was last pushed 2026-08-25. Eight releases (5.7.27-5.7.34) were uploaded to PyPI between 2026-06-29 and 2026-08-25. The last five releases (5.7.30-5.7.34) are infrastructure, documentation and citation changes: ARM64 wheels, the Bioinformatics citation, the docs theme and install workflows. BlueBrain/eFEL is archived (last push 2025-02-26). CHANGELOG.rst in the repo stops at 5.7.11 (2024-11), so release notes after that exist only as GitHub release pages.
windows_support: Supported in practice. PyPI has win_amd64 wheels for 5.7.34 on cp310-cp314 and cp314t. pyproject.toml contains a [tool.cibuildwheel.windows] test-command, so wheels are tested on Windows in CI. Verified locally: pip install efel==5.7.34 in a venv on Windows 11 with Python 3.12.10 installed cppcore.cp312-win_amd64.pyd, and feature extraction ran. Caveat: the PyPI trove classifiers list only 'Operating System :: MacOS' and 'Operating System :: POSIX'; there is no Windows classifier.

reuse_for_neurosem: Use efel==5.7.34 (pin exactly) as the feature-extraction backend in the M5 eFEL adapter via get_feature_values; do not reimplement spike detection, AP shape, ISI, adaptation, sag or burst features

Use eFEL's documented feature definitions (eFeatures.rst) as the citable operational definitions of each feature, and cite the Bioinformatics 2026 paper (DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btag328) plus the version DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19604220
Use the Settings dataclass (str(efel.get_settings())) as the serialisable record of Threshold, DerivativeThreshold, interp_step and the other extraction parameters for provenance
Use eFEL's None-on-failure convention as the source of 'undefined feature' status, propagated as an explicit missing value (never zero)
Use get_feature_names() to validate feature configuration and record the feature universe for the pinned version
Rely on the prebuilt win_amd64, manylinux and macOS wheels (no compiler needed) for M1 environment setup on Windows and in Docker/CI
Optionally use strict_stiminterval / spike_count_stimint for stimulus-window-restricted counting, and depol_block_bool for depolarisation-block detection
not_provided_new_for_neurosem: Unit conversion from jLEMS/jNeuroML .dat output (time in seconds; voltage inferred to be volts) to eFEL's ms/mV. eFEL does not detect wrong units and silently returns 0 spikes.

Mapping the LEMS/NeuroML stimulus definition (pulseGenerator delay and duration, ramps, rebound release) to stim_start and stim_end per protocol, including protocols where the analysis window differs from the stimulus window (rebound, zero-current baseline, paired pulses)
Rheobase search across multiple simulations (no rheobase feature in eFEL)
Qualitative firing-regime classification (tonic, adapting, bursting, rebound, silent, depolarisation block) built from eFEL features

Choosing and freezing one variant per handoff concept (e.g. steady_state_voltage_stimend vs steady_state_voltage, sag_ratio1 vs sag_ratio2, burst_number vs strict_burst_number) and defining per-spike aggregation (first, last, mean, count)

Per-protocol feature applicability rules (e.g. sag only for hyperpolarising steps, AP shape only when spike_count >= 1, ISI/adaptation only when enough spikes), since eFEL returns numbers for some features even where they are not meaningful

Three-state missing-value semantics for comparisons: defined vs undefined (None) vs legitimately zero, plus the rule for a feature defined in the reference but undefined in the mutant (and vice versa) as a detection event
Numerical-refinement tolerance calibration (h, h/2, h/4), common-grid trace alignment, trace-level metrics and the tau = max(abs floor, rel*|f|, c*|f_h - f_h/2|) rule. eFEL provides none of this.

Separating integration-step error from eFEL interp_step quantisation (time-based features are quantised to interp_step), e.g. by freezing interp_step at or below the finest recording interval and checking sensitivity
Settings isolation: guaranteeing efel.reset() plus explicit set_setting before each extraction, and rejecting unknown setting names that eFEL accepts silently
Capturing and logging eFEL RuntimeWarnings and DeprecationWarnings per run as diagnostics
Mutant generation, valid transformations, detection matrix, greedy and random protocol selection, held-out evaluation and leakage barriers
An evidence record linking each detection to protocol, feature, threshold and trace
handoff_assumption_issues: OUTDATED / needs updating: the handoff names eFEL without a location. The canonical repo is now openbraininstitute/eFEL (BlueBrain/eFEL is archived), and citation guidance now points to Bioinformatics 42(6) btag328 (2026) plus Zenodo concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19604220.

UNCERTAIN license wording: LICENSE.txt grants LGPL v3 or later (LGPL-3.0-or-later), but source file headers say version 3.0, PyPI says LGPLv3, Zenodo says lgpl-3.0, and GitHub reports NOASSERTION. LGPL is fine for a dependency but should be recorded as-is in LICENSE_AUDIT.md.

'Spike count': the eFEL name Spikecount is deprecated in 5.7.34 (DeprecationWarning; docs say it will be removed). Use spike_count (whole trace) or spike_count_stimint (in-stimulus); the two differ when spikes occur outside the window.

'Steady-state voltage' is ambiguous. eFEL's steady_state_voltage is the mean AFTER stimulus end; the during-stimulus steady state is steady_state_voltage_stimend. Using the literal name would silently measure the wrong window.

'Voltage deflection' has three eFEL variants with different windows (voltage_deflection uses 5 interpolated samples near stim_end; voltage_deflection_vb_ssse uses 10% windows; voltage_deflection_begin). The choice must be frozen.

'Sag ratio' has two eFEL definitions (sag_ratio1, sag_ratio2), and sag features returned finite values on a non-hyperpolarised spiking trace. Applicability must be restricted by protocol, or spurious differences may appear.

'Firing frequency': mean_frequency divides by (last in-stimulus spike time - stim_start), not stimulus duration, so one spike yields a nonzero rate. The handoff should specify which frequency definition is meant.
'First-spike latency': eFEL's time_to_first_spike is measured to the spike PEAK from stim_start. No 'latency' feature exists.

'AP amplitude' and 'AP half-width' are per-spike arrays in eFEL (AP_amplitude is relative to a derivative-threshold onset; AP_height is absolute). The handoff does not specify aggregation across spikes.

'First and last ISI': eFEL has no first_ISI/last_ISI features; use all_ISI_values[0] and [-1], or inv_first_ISI/inv_last_ISI (Hz). The deprecation chain is inconsistent (ISI_values says use ISIs; ISIs says use all_ISI_values), and ISI_values drops the first ISI by default (ignore_first_ISI=True).

'Never replace missing features with zero' is correct, but eFEL's docs are inconsistent: they say inv_first_ISI/inv_last_ISI return 0 when there is no ISI, while the 5.7.34 code returns None. eFEL itself returns array([0]) for counts (spike_count, burst_number) with no spikes. NeuroSem must pin the version and test the actual behaviour, not the docs.

'Burst count': burst_number and strict_burst_number disagreed on the same synthetic adapting train (0 vs 1); short trains print '4 or more spikes are needed for burst calculation'. The definition choice changes detections.
'Rheobase' is listed as a feature but is not an eFEL trace feature; it is a multi-simulation search that NeuroSem must implement and validate.
'Qualitative firing regime' is not provided by eFEL as a single feature; it is NeuroSem logic built on eFEL outputs.

'Record interpolation' is necessary but understated. eFEL always linearly resamples to interp_step (default 0.1 ms) regardless of the jNeuroML recording interval, and time-based features (e.g. half-width) are quantised to that step. In the h, h/2, h/4 refinement, feature differences can reflect interp_step quantisation or the recording interval rather than integration error, so interp_step must be frozen and its sensitivity checked. If the LEMS recording interval is coarser than interp_step, interpolation cannot recover peak shape.

Units are unaddressed in the handoff. jLEMS .dat time is in seconds (per the pyNeuroML docstring) while eFEL assumes ms/mV (Threshold -20, interp_step 0.1 ms). Unconverted SI traces silently give 0 spikes; a mixed-unit trace (T in s) makes interp_step mean 0.1 s.

Default spike Threshold -20 mV can miss low-amplitude spikes in some models (verified synthetically); a fixed global threshold vs a per-model frozen threshold is a decision to make before the discovery analysis.

Rebound / post-stimulus protocols: eFEL's trace_check treats spikes after 1.05*stim_end as an invalid trace, and features such as mean_frequency and adaptation_index only consider in-stimulus spikes. Rebound spikes need a deliberate analysis-window design (e.g. separate stim_start/stim_end for the post-release window).

eFEL settings are process-global mutable state and accept unknown setting names silently; parallel extraction or a forgotten reset() can contaminate results. The handoff's reproducibility rules should require reset-per-extraction and setting-name validation.
uncertainties: The jNeuroML/LEMS output voltage unit (volts) is inferred from pyNeuroML's x1000 conversion, not from a LEMS/jNeuroML specification statement. The docs.neuroml.org LEMSSimulation page did not state output units. Needs confirmation by the jNeuroML audit or a real fixture run.
